questions.q: Where do you start analyzing a log?
options: With an abrupt log end and vibration
With GPS quality and the satellite count over the whole flight
questions.explain: A log that ends abruptly means a power loss; high vibration devalues everything else.

questions.q: What is the VIBE limit above which altitude and position problems are almost certain?
questions.explain: Below 30 is normal, above 60 almost certainly means problems.

questions.q: An ERR with Subsys 17, ECode 1 is…
options: Loss of the radio link to the transmitter
questions.explain: 2 is radio, 11 is GPS, 16 is EKF variance, 17 is the EKF failsafe, 29 is vibration compensation.

questions.q: Which ATT fields do you compare to spot a mechanical problem?
questions.explain: A sharp divergence between desired and actual means a failure or a lack of thrust.

options: Telemetry as the GCS saw it
An ESC firmware log with telemetry
questions.explain: The telemetry the GCS saw over the radio: lower rate and with gaps, but it survives even if the SD card burned.

questions.q: What do you read a .bin with in Python?
CTUN.ThO = 0.78 with sagging voltage in Loiter indicates:
questions.explain: The throttle is at the ceiling with sagging voltage; BAT.Volt/Curr confirm it.

questions.q: What do you enable for PID tuning?
options: Only GPS and the IMU at full rate
questions.explain: PID (PIDR/PIDP/PIDY) is already in the default mask, but at 10 Hz; bit 0, Fast Attitude, logs ANG/RATE/PID at the loop rate, and batch sampling (INS_LOG_BAT_MASK, not a LOG_BITMASK bit) gives the spectrum for the filters. Only while tuning; turn them off afterwards, because the log grows.
